sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Type / MCQs / Assertion-Reasoning

questions.question_text: Which component of food acts mainly as the primary energy provider for our body?
questions.answer: C) Carbohydrates

questions.question_text: Which of the following materials is generally considered a good electrical insulator?
questions.answer: C) Rubber band

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): A piece of chalk is softer than a piece of iron.
Reason (R): Materials that can be easily compressed or scratched are classified as soft materials.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text: Which type of motion does a plucked string of a guitar exhibit?
questions.answer: C) Periodic or oscillatory motion

questions.question_text: Which part of a typical plant is primarily responsible for absorbing water and dissolved minerals from the soil?
questions.answer: C) Root

questions.question_text: A magnet will most strongly attract objects made from which of the following materials?
questions.answer: C) Iron

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Transparent materials allow light to pass through them completely.
Reason (R): Oiled paper is an example of a perfectly transparent material.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: C) A is true but R is false.

questions.question_text: Which of the following units is the standard SI unit for measuring length?
questions.answer: C) Meter

questions.question_text: What happens when the North pole of one magnet is brought near the North pole of another freely suspended magnet?
options: A) They strongly attract each other.
C) They neither attract nor repel.
D) One magnet loses its magnetism completely.
questions.answer: B) They repel each other.

questions.question_text: The disease 'Goiter', characterized by swelling in the neck region, is caused by the deficiency of which mineral?
questions.answer: C) Iodine

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Measuring length using a handspan gives identical results for every student in a class.
Reason (R): Standard units of measurement are necessary because body parts vary in size from person to person.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: D) A is false but R is true.

questions.question_text: Which of these living organisms is known to breathe through specialized structures called gills?
questions.answer: C) Fish

questions.question_text: Materials that sink in water generally have what property compared to water?
options: A) They are less dense than water.
B) They are more dense than water.
C) They are highly soluble in water.
questions.answer: B) They are more dense than water.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of roughage (dietary fiber) in our diet?
options: B) It provides instant high energy.
C) It helps the body get rid of undigested food and prevents constipation.
questions.answer: C) It helps the body get rid of undigested food and prevents constipation.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): When a bar magnet is cut into two equal halves, you get two complete magnets, each with a North and South pole.
Reason (R): Magnetic poles always exist in pairs and cannot be isolated.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.question_text: In a flowering plant, which part develops into a fruit after pollination and fertilization?
questions.answer: C) Ovary

questions.question_text: A car moving on a perfectly straight highway without changing direction is an example of what type of motion?
questions.answer: C) Rectilinear motion

questions.question_text: Which of the following food items is a rich source of both proteins and fats?
questions.answer: C) Eggs

questions.question_text: Where is the magnetic strength of a bar magnet generally the strongest?
options: C) Only at the North pole
D) At both of its poles
questions.answer: D) At both of its poles

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Sugar dissolves completely when stirred into a glass of water.
Reason (R): Materials that mix completely in water are termed as insoluble substances.
Choose the correct option:
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
C) A is true but R is false.
D) A is false but R is true.
questions.answer: C) A is true but R is false.

questions.question_text: List any two distinct properties that can be used to group or sort materials in daily life. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Materials can be grouped based on their appearance (like luster or color), transparency (whether light passes through), or solubility (whether they dissolve in water).

questions.question_text: Name the primary vitamin that helps our body absorb calcium, and state one natural source of it. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Vitamin D is essential for the absorption of calcium in the body. A major natural source of Vitamin D is direct exposure to morning sunlight.

questions.question_text: Why do measuring tapes made of elastic or stretchable material give incorrect length measurements? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Elastic tapes can stretch while measuring, causing the marked numbers to spread apart. This inconsistency leads to highly inaccurate and varying length measurements every time.

questions.question_text: What happens to the magnetic properties of a magnet if it is repeatedly dropped on a hard floor or heated strongly? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Repeated dropping, hammering, or strong heating disrupts the alignment of magnetic domains inside, causing the magnet to lose its magnetic strength and properties permanently.

questions.question_text: Define the term 'habitat' and give one example of an aquatic habitat. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A habitat is the natural environment where a plant or animal lives, finds food, and survives. A common example of an aquatic habitat is a freshwater pond.

questions.question_text: Identify the type of motion demonstrated by the blades of a moving ceiling fan and the needle of a running sewing machine. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The blades of a ceiling fan exhibit circular motion as they rotate around a fixed center. The needle of a sewing machine shows periodic or oscillatory motion.

questions.question_text: Explain the iodine test used to confirm the presence of starch in a food sample. What color change indicates a positive result? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: To test for starch, add a few drops of dilute iodine solution to the crushed food sample. If the food turns a distinct blue-black color, it positively indicates the presence of starch.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between transparent, translucent, and opaque materials, giving one example of each. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Transparent materials (like clear glass) let light pass entirely. Translucent materials (like frosted glass or butter paper) let light pass only partially. Opaque materials (like wood) completely block all light from passing through.

questions.question_text: Describe the proper procedure and precautions for using a meter scale to measure the exact length of a wooden block. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Place the scale perfectly parallel to the block's edge. Align the zero mark with the block's starting edge. Ensure your eye is positioned directly vertically above the reading point to avoid parallax errors during measurement.

questions.question_text: How can you use a simple bar magnet to find geographical directions if you are lost in an unfamiliar place? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Suspend the bar magnet freely using a thread tied to its center. Once it stops swinging, it will naturally align itself in the North-South direction. The end pointing towards the geographic North is the magnet's North pole.

questions.question_text: Briefly explain the functions of the stem and the leaves in a plant's survival and growth. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The stem supports the plant upright and transports water from roots to leaves. Leaves act as the plant's food factory, performing photosynthesis by using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to produce nutrients.

questions.question_text: What is a balanced diet? Why is it crucial for a growing child to consume a balanced diet daily? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: A balanced diet contains the right proportions of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and roughage. It is crucial for children because it provides the necessary energy, supports rapid physical growth, and builds immunity against diseases.

questions.question_text: Describe an activity to prove that magnetic force can pass through non-magnetic materials like paper or plastic. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Place a few iron nails on top of a plastic sheet. Move a strong magnet underneath the sheet. The nails will move along with the magnet, proving that magnetic lines of force penetrate the non-magnetic plastic.

questions.question_text: A student claims that a rolling ball shows only one type of motion. Correct this statement by explaining the dual motions involved. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The statement is incorrect because a rolling ball exhibits two motions simultaneously. It shows rectilinear motion as it moves straight forward across the ground, and circular (rotational) motion as it continuously turns around its own center.

questions.question_text: Read the case context: During a science fair, a group of students mixed iron filings, sulfur powder, and small pebbles in a tray. They were asked to separate these three components completely without using water. Describe a step-by-step physical separation method they should use, explaining the underlying property exploited at each step. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, the students should use a strong magnet and hover it over the mixture; the magnetic iron filings will be attracted and separated out. Next, they should use a sieve with a mesh size smaller than the pebbles. The fine sulfur powder will pass through the sieve holes, leaving the larger pebbles trapped behind, achieving complete separation based on magnetism and particle size.

questions.question_text: Compare the tap root system with the fibrous root system in plants. Describe their physical differences and explain how the type of root system correlates with the venation pattern found in the plant's leaves. Provide one example of a plant for each system. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: A tap root has one main thick root growing deep with smaller lateral roots, typically found in plants with reticulate (net-like) leaf venation, like a mustard or rose plant. A fibrous root system consists of many thin, equal-sized roots spreading out near the surface, corresponding to plants with parallel leaf venation, such as grass, wheat, or maize.

questions.question_text: While organizing a dark storeroom, Amit finds an unlabelled metal bar. He suspects it is a magnet. He is given another verified bar magnet with marked North and South poles. Detail the exact experimental steps Amit must perform to conclusively prove whether his metal bar is a permanent magnet or just a piece of ordinary iron. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Amit should bring the known North pole of the verified magnet near both ends of the unlabelled bar, one by one. If both ends of the unlabelled bar are attracted, it is merely a piece of ordinary magnetic iron. However, if one end strongly repels the known North pole, the unlabelled bar is definitely a permanent magnet, because repulsion is the only sure test of magnetism.

questions.question_text: Malnutrition can lead to severe deficiency diseases. A child exhibits symptoms of poor vision in darkness, bleeding gums, and soft, easily bendable bones. Identify the three specific vitamin or mineral deficiencies causing these symptoms. Recommend a specific type of food for each deficiency that the child must include in their diet to recover. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Poor night vision indicates Vitamin A deficiency, which can be cured by eating carrots or papaya. Bleeding gums point to Vitamin C deficiency (Scurvy), treatable by consuming citrus fruits like amla or oranges. Soft bones indicate Vitamin D or Calcium deficiency (Rickets), requiring increased intake of milk, dairy products, or exposure to morning sunlight.
